Use case: stylized-concept. Produce one original square transparent Artwork asset for Glaze Facetlight Pinewood. The subject is one whole familiar pine cone in a straight-on botanical specimen view with a gentle diagonal tilt. Give it a naturally tapered egg-shaped outline, a complete short stem, and about five staggered rows of broad overlapping scales with irregular rounded tips. Keep the whole cone and stem inside the central 70 percent of the square. Leave at least 15 percent true transparent exterior on each side. The subject should read as a pine cone immediately at 85 px.

Build the entire cone as a flat false-color image of surface direction, inspired by the appearance of an RGB normal map. Show one repeating direction relationship on each visible scale. A broad flat-facing center is periwinkle, a left-facing shoulder transitions to cyan, a right-facing shoulder transitions to warm rose, and an upward-facing lip carries a thin pale mint field. The same direction should receive the same color wherever it appears, regardless of the scale's height or distance from the center. Smooth matte changes within each scale reset crisply at the true visible overlap with the next scale. Make the directional colors readable in the central scales and tighter toward the side tips. Use a restrained, relatively even brightness across the image. Avoid a whole-cone rainbow sweep. Local color changes should trace the anatomy of individual scales, with no valleys painted as dark ambient shadows.

This is a flat direction image with fully opaque color fields inside the silhouette. Show the outline and scale forms through their contours and color changes. Keep it free of wood grain, paper fibers, pigment strokes, metal highlights, finish reflections, glossy gradients, glitter, specular spots, soft cast shadows, heavy borders, light halos or halo haze. Avoid pearlescent drainage swirls, irregular black windows, wavy stress fringes, thermographic gradients, shattered mosaic grains or a projected stripe pattern. The stem is short and simple, using the same direction colors. Do not make a pine cone assembled from plastic or carved stone. This is original artistic false color, with no real measurement, dataset, texture calibration, model or sensor readout.

Use genuine alpha transparency outside the whole cone and stem. No backing rectangle, floor, frame, labels, coordinates, ruler, text, numbers, live widget readings, UI, logo or watermark. No external visual inputs.

Use the same directional colors across the shoulder, cheek, bill and twig to define their shape.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the single exact own Facetlight Pinewood wallpaper. Preserve this portrait scene's size, framing, matte slate background, wide empty side margins, quiet upper and lower fields, and all five existing original subjects. Keep the whole pine cone and stem, woodpecker and complete short twig, three shelf fungi and the complete bark fragment, squirrel silhouette including paws and raised tail, and columbine flower, bud and both divided leaves. Preserve their positions, proportions, contours and exact existing four-color patterns. Do not move or resize any whole subject.

Make two subtle local composition changes only. The bottom of the long columbine stalk appears to enter the squirrel's head. Starting below the stem's existing leaf junction, curve the lower stem gently left into the narrow space between the pine cone and squirrel, ending at the existing mint ground line. Keep a visible small gap between this stalk and the squirrel's ears, snout, paws and body. If there is very little room, make the part of the stalk nearest the feet thin. Keep all upper plant parts exactly as they are. Second, suggest one short forest tree surface behind the woodpecker twig and shelf fungi with two very quiet, low contrast slate contour strokes. The strokes align the twig and the bark into the same little woodland scene, with their endpoints ending softly inside the group. They must stay muted enough that the original five colorful shapes remain dominant. No added saturated patches, large solid trunk, shading, texture or grain.

Preserve the original spacing and whole silhouettes, all subject endpoints, and the quiet edges of the wallpaper. No crop, new flowers, animals, leaves, duplicate subjects, text, labels, border, logo or watermark. This remains one full opaque portrait wallpaper.

Retain the broad flat directional colors of the five references. The periwinkle face, cyan left shoulder, rose right shoulder and mint upward lip change at each actual local fold or overlap. Keep the same clean flat graphic fields inside each familiar natural shape. No physical sheen, ordinary reflected light, grain or texture. This is an artistic convention inspired by surface direction images, with no actual data, calibration or sensor readout.

Set all five subjects together in a single small woodland vignette. A gentle line suggesting the forest floor ties the scene together. Place the woodpecker higher left, gripping its complete short twig. The three shelf fungi sit below it on their whole short bark fragment. The complete columbine stalk rises to the right with its open flower, bud and divided leaves. A whole squirrel rests low right with an uncropped broad raised tail and its feet visible. A whole standing pine cone rests near the bottom center with its short stem. Use a few tiny dark slate needles to suggest a woodland floor and give each subject a little negative space. Keep the exact familiar shape of each reference and preserve the whole bill, twig, tail, fungi lips, flowers and cone. Arrange the five forms at varied heights and sizes within one coherent scene. Keep each of the five distinctive silhouettes separate and avoid repeating any of them.
